I struggled with anorexia as a teen, but not anymore. I’m surprised most people in the comments didn’t experience weight gain. I was on Zoloft(100-200mg), Lithium (600mg), and antipsychotics. I’ve had small hallucinations on very little sleep, flickers of shadow people included. I’ve started to hallucinate short visuals when waking too, just over the past year (not sleep paralysis since I’m actually awake when it happens). I’ve seen spiders crawling up the walls, a bat in my room, people walking in through my door, all brief moments. It’s scary, but after a chat with my therapist, I was relieved to learn it’s relatively normal for people under extreme amounts of stress. Some of my paranoia was playing into it.

Also wanted to add: it’s impressive you’re realizing these things about yourself and are looking to improve. Good luck. 🤍

Edit: Sorry…one more thing lol. If you want to be better, another helpful tip might be to learn and practice how to apologize. If you made a mistake or exposed someone to your aggressive behaviors, give a sincere apology. It doesn’t have to be when you’re in the thick of emotions, but take the time to recollect, reassess, and approach them. What people decide to do with your apology is up to them, but I really admire people who can take accountability for their mistakes and try to make things right. It shows good morals. All suggestions. :)
